Marker-mode usability checklist (manual, development-only — not a chemistry test)

This checklist documents what a first-time marker should be able to identify at each stage, as a manual review aid. It creates no fixture data of its own and does not affect the decision-engine or isolation tests below.

  • Empty app test — on a freshly reset project, can a new user identify: where the method specifications go (section A), where the starting conditions go (section B), and where the CSV upload goes (section C)? See the numbered "1 / 2 / 3" setup-order labels on section A and the "What should I do now?" panel at the top of the Dashboard.
  • Normal automatic-decision test — after a regular retention-ladder upload, can a new user identify the decision, the reason ("Why?" under section E), and the next run conditions (section G)?
  • Human-judgement test — at an OBSERVE state (retention or second-solvent), can a new user identify that a choice is required of them, and which evidence they should compare, from the "Human judgement required" labelling?
  • Terminal test — at MET or a Efficiency/N hand-off, can a new user identify whether FC1 is complete or has been handed off, from the "What should I do now?" panel and section G?
  • Auto-fill / expected-condition test (Sections C & D) — after any run/human-action that generates a real next-run recommendation, is it obvious from section B's own banner that Section B has been pre-filled from that recommendation (the exact "Pre-filled from the previous FC1 recommendation..." label)? And if a later upload's own recorded conditions do not match that frozen expectation, is it obvious from the Decision card and the Next Run Conditions card exactly which fields differ and what to do about it (correct section B and re-upload, or confirm a new/different workflow)?

Retention & Selectivity

This tab shows progress for the chemistry / workflow instance matching the Current Chemistry / Run Conditions form (section B) on the Dashboard. Use the Selectivity Sequence card (card I) on the Dashboard to act on the current step -- the second-solvent nomogram %B is generated and applied automatically (no manual entry), so no %B has to be typed by hand.

Judgement steps in Selectivity. Official BPS2032 course workflow: 40°C → 60°C in the first solvent → automatic nomogram solvent change → ambient, 40°C, 60°C in the second solvent → the final optional-temperature OBSERVE (test one extra temperature, 20–60°C, or not) → the ligand change (select the next ligand). Added by this app as optional study aids, not mandatory official BPS2032 steps: an OBSERVE question after the first-solvent 40°C run and an OBSERVE question after the second-solvent 40°C run (“Did changing the temperature move the peaks in the desired direction?” — Yes continues to 60°C; No skips that 60°C run). See Help → “OBSERVE steps”.

Help / How to Use

FIRST-TIME USER — NORMAL WORKFLOW

  1. Enter the method specifications in Section A on the Dashboard.
  2. Enter the first-run HPLC conditions in Section B.
  3. Upload the completed chromatography CSV in Section C.
  4. Read the Decision in Section E and its "Why?".
  5. Set the HPLC exactly to the Next Run Conditions in Section G.
  6. Run the experiment, export the new CSV, and upload it.
  7. Repeat until the app says MET or hand off to Efficiency (N).

Most of the time, this is all you need to do.

If a purple HUMAN JUDGEMENT REQUIRED box appears, stop and make the requested choice yourself. The app will show the evidence but will not choose for you.

What this tool does

This app walks one HPLC method through FC1 (Retention, then Selectivity) to a decision: MET, or a hand-off to Efficiency (Flow Chart 2). It runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded to a server, and your project data is kept only in this browser's local storage.

Quick start

  1. Enter the method specifications (section A).
  2. Enter the conditions of the first run (section B).
  3. Upload the CSV (section C).
  4. Read the Decision (section E) and its "Why?" explanation.
  5. Set the HPLC to the Next Run Conditions (section G) and run it.
  6. Repeat from step 3 until FC1 exits to MET or Efficiency (N).

The "What should I do now?" panel at the top of the Dashboard always states the single next action in plain language.

What the four run-summary values mean

Peak count — derived by counting valid Peak Table rows; determines whether the target peak count has been reached.
Last tR — directly reported/read from the last valid Peak Table retention time; used in Retention/run-time decisions.
Minimum Rs — derived by selecting the minimum eligible value from software-reported Rs values; only becomes decisive once the target peak count is reached.
Back pressure — derived by this app from the reported Pump A pressure trace; checked first as the safety gate.

Automatic vs human decisions

Most states are calculated automatically from the parsed values and the method specifications — the retention ladder, Min%B, and the temperature/solvent steps of Selectivity (including the automatic nomogram-converted solvent switch). A few states need your judgement instead: OBSERVE (retention, second-solvent) and the ligand change. Those are marked Human judgement required — the app shows the evidence but does not pick a value for you.

Resolution when the peak count is below target. Shown as “Rs = 0 — not assessable” (a status convention, not a measurement); the reported value is kept beside it and is never used in a calculation. With no Rs in the CSV it reads “Rs not assessable — no Rs reported”.

Changing the Method Specifications. After you edit Section A, the latest run is re-assessed against the new specifications without adding a run; its upload-time specifications and decision are kept. If the change conflicts with a choice you already made, the app asks you to reconfirm instead of overriding it.

Chromatograms. Open Equipment Explorer and scroll to the last section, Explore a Chromatogram. The latest uploaded run is shown by default; use the Selected run dropdown to view any earlier run. In Run History, the View chromatogram link under each run label opens Equipment Explorer with that run selected. Viewing a chromatogram is display only: it never changes the current run, the decision or the next-run recommendation. Runs uploaded before V38, or CSVs without a chromatogram section, show an “unavailable” message — nothing is generated.

OBSERVE steps: official course steps vs study aids

OBSERVE stepWhere it appearsStatus
Retention OBSERVE (choose an intermediate %B or the run to take into Selectivity)After the Min%B run, when the peak count is still below targetOfficial BPS2032 workflow (the “Observe” figure after Min%B in the flow chart)
Final optional-temperature OBSERVE (test one extra temperature, 20–60°C, or go to the ligand change)After the second-solvent temperature runsOfficial BPS2032 workflow (the “Observe / other deg” step in the flow chart)
OBSERVE after the first-solvent 40°C runSelectivity card (I), after the 40°C run in the first organic solventOptional study aid added in this app — not a course requirement
OBSERVE after the second-solvent 40°C runSelectivity card (I), after the 40°C run in the second organic solventOptional study aid added in this app — not a course requirement

Why the 40°C questions are asked. Temperature is the first Selectivity parameter. After the first 40°C run in each organic solvent, the app asks you to look at the chromatogram and judge: “Did changing the temperature move the chromatographic peaks in the desired direction?” This encourages deliberate observation before committing the next run. The question is asked again after the second-solvent 40°C run because the new solvent changes selectivity, so the effect of temperature has to be judged afresh.

YES — temperature is moving the peaks the right way: the default course sequence continues to the 60°C run (already pre-filled in Section B and shown in Next Run Conditions).

NO — the 60°C run is skipped (recorded as “Skipped — OBSERVE answered NO”). After the first-solvent 40°C run, the app moves straight to the second organic solvent at the automatic nomogram-equivalent %B, ambient temperature (same conversion as usual). After the second-solvent 40°C run, the app moves to the official final optional-temperature OBSERVE (no third solvent), and then the ligand change.

While an answer is pending, the 60°C conditions are shown labelled “Pending OBSERVE confirmation” and later Selectivity steps read “Not yet available — awaiting OBSERVE answer”. If you upload the default 60°C CSV without answering, it is accepted (the course order is 40°C then 60°C) and recorded as “not answered” — never as Yes. Uploading the NO-path conditions without answering NO is refused. In a multi-file queue, processing pauses at the 40°C file; the remaining files wait unevaluated and continue automatically once you answer.

Note: the official sequence and rubric run 40°C then 60°C before changing solvent; answering NO is a deliberate, recorded deviation from that order.

What happens when target peaks are reached

Once peak count reaches the target, %B and Selectivity are frozen: a full tR/Rs pass is classified MET (FC1 complete); any other tR/Rs outcome hands off directly to Efficiency (N), outside FC1 scope, per the locked forum-priority target-peak policy.

Common problems

CSV unreadable / empty Peak Table — the run is recorded for audit but cannot be evaluated.
What to do: check that the correct LabSolutions-style export was uploaded, then re-upload it.

Back pressure unavailable — Evaluation is blocked at the first gate.
What to do: check that the correct LabSolutions CSV was exported and that the Pump A pressure trace is present, then re-upload.

Missing Rs — No trustworthy reported Rs values were available in the Peak Table, so minimum Rs cannot be derived. Below the target peak count, Rs is reference-only; once the target peak count is reached, a trustworthy Rs result is required for the final tR/Rs classification.
What to do: check the Peak Table's Resolution column in the exported CSV; re-export if it looks incomplete.

Duplicate upload — the app flags a file it believes was already uploaded.
What to do: confirm whether this really is a new run before proceeding.

Metadata conflict — the file's internal sample-name metadata disagrees with the Current Chemistry form; nothing is overwritten automatically.
What to do: check which one is correct before proceeding.

More peaks than target (INVESTIGATE) — flagged for manual review rather than silently continued.
What to do: review the run yourself before deciding how to continue.
